environment: Chrome DevTools MCP (Chromium 156 UA), desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844, normal network/CPU, anonymous user session only.
verdict: Core anonymous browse flows passed; one confirmed functional availability failure on Penang destination listing (HTTP 503).

coverage.input: Continue to reservation from hotel page
Sort by price low to high

coverage.expected: Reject expired code with clear feedback
coverage.actual: Inline alert + API 422 with request id shown
Nav, filters, cards rendered and interactive
Focus moved through main nav links

findings.title: Penang destination query returns unavailable state (HTTP 503)
findings.impact: Users cannot browse Penang destination inventory in the discover flow, reducing bookable destination coverage.
preconditions: Destination, pool filter, and sort controls visible
steps: Keep pool=true and sort=price low to high
findings.expected: Destination filter should return matching Penang stays data or a recoverable fallback.
findings.expected_basis: UI destination filter semantics and successful responses for the same flow with other destinations.
findings.actual: UI shows results unavailable and returns HTTP 503 from hotels listing API.
findings.comparison: Equivalent Langkawi query returned 200 and rendered 3 stays.

limitations: No authenticated test account was supplied; signed-in flows are blocked.
DevTools screenshot file-save paths were restricted in this session, so evidence files were not persisted to disk.
next_checks: Retest Penang with pool=false and alternate sort modes to isolate whether the outage is destination-only or condition-specific.
Run full authenticated booking journey once credentials are available.
Collect at least three comparable timing samples for hotels and quote endpoints.
